Question: Which is the first day of the course that does not take place on campus?
Hint: There are two different 'firsts': the first day that is not on campus, and the first live online class one day later.

Question: A student has 85 for continuous work and 78 on the Mid-term. With the weights of the syllabus, how many of the 100 grade points are earned before the Final?
Hint: Multiply each mark by its weight (0.30 and 0.30), then add the two products.

Question: In which order do the five beats of every lecture part run?
Hint: The explanation comes first, then the picture, then your hands, then your memory, then a rest.

Question: A student wants to practise on the customer list of the shop where she works. Which ground rule decides, and what is the correct action?
Hint: Whose names and addresses are in that list?
a: No recording: she may use the list if she does not record the class
b: Fictional or open data only: she must not load it, and uses Mercadillo 505 or an approved open dataset
c: Honest work: she may use the list if she cites the shop in APA (American Psychological Association) style
d: No rule applies, because the data stay on her own laptop

Question: Which statements about the two exams are true? (select 3)
Hint: Add the two weights, then recall the wording of the agreement.
a: Both are held on campus, in person
b: Both are invigilated by another professor
c: Together they are worth 70 % of the course grade
d: The Mid-term can be taken online from home
e: The Final covers only Classes 9 to 12
f: They are formative and do not count

Question: Which conditions must a dataset of your own meet before it may replace the Mercadillo 505 starter file? (select 3)
Hint: Three conditions: the right to use the data, privacy, and enough content for three tables.
a: An open licence that you can name
b: No personal information about real people
c: At least 1,000 rows that describe at least three kinds of thing
d: It must come from your employer
e: It must already be stored in PostgreSQL
f: It must contain at least one million rows

Question: Which line is information, in the sense used in this lecture?
Hint: Information is data processed and placed in a context. It is neither the raw record nor the action taken afterwards.
c: The column quantity must be greater than zero
d: Send the second van to Madrid next Saturday

Question: A customer's city is stored in the orders file and in the customers file. The customer moves, and only one file is updated. Which pair of terms names the cause and the result?
Hint: First one fact is stored twice. Then the two copies disagree.
b: Program-data dependence, then limited data sharing

Question: Which statement describes the DBMS (Database Management System) correctly?
Hint: Keep three things apart: the stored data, the software that controls access to them, and the programs that use them.
a: It is the organised collection of stored data
b: It is the program that draws the sales chart for the manager
c: It is the software through which every read and every write of the stored data passes
d: It is the person who makes the backups

Question: A column is declared NOT NULL. A user tries to save a row in which that value is empty. What does the DBMS (Database Management System) do?
Hint: A constraint is checked at every insertion, before the row is stored.
a: It saves the row and stores a zero
b: It saves the row and warns the administrator later
c: It refuses the row and returns an error — for every user and every application
d: It deletes the other rows that have empty values

Question: Which of the following are problems of keeping business data in separate files and spreadsheets? (select 3)
Hint: Three options are weaknesses of files; the other three are what the database approach offers instead.

Question: Which are responsibilities of a DBMS (Database Management System) named in this lecture? (select 4)
Hint: The DBMS (Database Management System) stores, checks, coordinates and restores. It does not choose the questions and it does not present the answers.
f: Drawing the charts of the report

Question: A file-based (embedded) database differs from a flat file because it …
Hint: Think of SQLite and DuckDB: no server, one file, and a complete query language.
a: is stored on a server that must be started first
b: is a complete DBMS (Database Management System) that runs inside the program and keeps the database in one file
d: cannot be queried with SQL (Structured Query Language)

Question: Which family is the usual choice for a bank's account transfers, and why?
Hint: One organisation owns the data, and a transfer must debit one account and credit another together.
a: Key-value, because a lookup by account number is fast
b: Relational, because constraints and transactions keep related rows correct under many simultaneous writers
c: Big data, because a bank has many customers

Question: In a blockchain, what makes the alteration of an old entry detectable?
Hint: A hash is computed from the entire content of a block.
a: The entry is protected by a password
b: Each block stores the hash of the previous block, so a changed block no longer matches the value stored in the next one
c: Old blocks are deleted after one day
d: Only one administrator is allowed to write

Question: The source code of a product can be read by anyone, but its licence forbids offering the product as a service to others. Is it open-source software in the sense used in this course?
Hint: Source code that is visible and a licence that is open are two different things.
a: Yes, because the source code is visible
b: Yes, if the product is free of charge
c: No: the licence must allow use for any purpose, modification and redistribution, and be approved by the OSI (Open Source Initiative)
d: No, because companies may never use open-source software

Question: Which of the following are kinds of non-relational database? (select 4)
Hint: There are four kinds, each named after its data model.

Question: 400 sensors each send one reading every 10 seconds, and analysts need monthly summaries over several years. Which two techniques of the big-data family answer this need? (select 2)
Hint: One technique reads only the columns that are needed; the other divides the work among many machines.
a: Columnar storage, for example Apache Parquet
b: Distributed processing, for example Apache Spark
e: A CHECK constraint on the city
f: Saving the readings in a spreadsheet
